title: The three t-tests, their formulas and the t table
summary: One-sample, independent two-sample and paired t-tests: when each is used, the formula for each (including pooled SD), and how the deck reads critical values from the t-distribution table.

chunks.heading: Which t-test when
chunks.explanation_md:
**One-Sample t-Test**
- Compares the **mean of a single group** to a **known or hypothesised population mean**.
- Used when you want to know if **your sample is significantly different from a specific value**.

**Independent Two-Sample t-Test (Unpaired)**
- Compares the **means of two independent groups**.
- Used when samples come from **different populations** (e.g. **Treatment vs Control**).
- The **groups must be unrelated**.

**Paired (Dependent) t-Test**
- Compares the means from the **same group at different times (pre/post)** or **matched pairs**.
- Used when **measurements are repeated** or **pairs are naturally linked**.

Quick test: one group vs a number, one-sample; two unrelated groups, independent; same people twice, paired.

chunks.heading: The three formulas
chunks.explanation_md:
**One-sample t-test**

t = (x̄ − μ0) / (s/√n)

where **x̄** is the sample mean, **μ0** the hypothesized population mean, **s** the standard deviation and **n** the sample size.

**Independent two-sample t-test (assume equal variances)**

t = (x̄1 − x̄2) / (sp √(1/n1 + 1/n2))

where the **pooled standard deviation** is

sp = √[((n1 − 1)s1² + (n2 − 1)s2²) / (n1 + n2 − 2)]

**Paired t-test**

First compute the **difference for each pair**: di = x1,i − x2,i. Then

t = d̄ / (sd/√n)

where **d̄** is the mean of the differences, **sd** the standard deviation of the differences and **n** the **number of pairs**.

key_terms.meaning: sp = √[((n1 − 1)s1² + (n2 − 1)s2²) / (n1 + n2 − 2)], used in the independent two-sample t-test assuming equal variances.

chunks.exam_line: One-sample t = (x̄ − μ0)/(s/√n); independent t = (x̄1 − x̄2)/(sp√(1/n1 + 1/n2)) with pooled sp; paired t = d̄/(sd/√n), n = number of pairs.

chunks.heading: Reading the t-distribution table
chunks.explanation_md:
The **t-distribution table** lists **degrees of freedom (df)** down the side (1 to 30, then 40 up to 1000 and Infinite) and nine column headings across: **0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05, 0.025, 0.01, 0.005, 0.001, 0.0005**. The 0.05 column is shaded.

**How the worked examples in this deck read it:**
- **Two-tailed test at α = 0.05**: the **0.025** column. For df = 9 that is **2.685**; for df = 27 it is **2.373**.
- **One-tailed test at α = 0.05**: the **0.05** column. For df = 5 that is **2.571**.

Note: in these three examples the decision line still prints an older number (2.262, 2.052 and 2.015); in each one the decision is the same with either number.

questions.stem: Differentiate between the one-sample, independent two-sample and paired t-tests.
questions.model_answer_md:
The three t-tests answer different questions about means.

| Test | Compares | Use when | Formula |
|---|---|---|---|
| **One-sample** | Mean of a single group with a **known or hypothesised population mean** | You want to know if your sample differs from a specific value | t = (x̄ − μ0)/(s/√n) |
| **Independent two-sample (unpaired)** | Means of **two independent groups** | Samples come from different populations, e.g. Treatment vs Control; groups must be unrelated | t = (x̄1 − x̄2)/(sp √(1/n1 + 1/n2)) |
| **Paired (dependent)** | Means from the **same group at different times** (pre/post) or **matched pairs** | Measurements are repeated or pairs are naturally linked | t = d̄/(sd/√n) |

The key question is whether there is one group, two unrelated groups, or linked pairs.

rubric.point: One-sample: single mean vs known value
Independent: two unrelated groups, e.g. Treatment vs Control
Paired: same group pre/post or matched pairs

questions.stem: Using the pulse data (before: 72, 75, 70, 80, 78, 77; after: 70, 76, 69, 78, 76, 75), compute the differences, their mean d̄ and their standard deviation sd.
questions.model_answer_md:
The paired t-test starts from the difference for each client.

**Differences (before − after):** 72 − 70 = 2; 75 − 76 = −1; 70 − 69 = 1; 80 − 78 = 2; 78 − 76 = 2; 77 − 75 = 2.

**Mean difference:** d̄ = (2 − 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 2)/6 = 8/6 ≈ **1.33**

**Standard deviation of differences:**
- Deviations from 1.33: 0.67, −2.33, −0.33, 0.67, 0.67, 0.67
- Squares: 0.44, 5.44, 0.11, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44; sum ≈ **7.33**
- Divide by n − 1 = 5: 7.33/5 ≈ **1.467**
- sd = √1.467 ≈ **1.211**

**Answer:** differences 2, −1, 1, 2, 2, 2; **d̄ ≈ 1.33**; **sd ≈ 1.211**, matching the slide.

rubric.point: Sum of squared deviations ≈ 7.33, divided by n − 1

questions.stem: For Class A (n = 15, SD = 10) and Class B (n = 14, SD = 8), calculate the pooled standard deviation using the slide's formula.
questions.model_answer_md:
The pooled SD combines the two groups' variability, assuming equal variances.

**Formula:** sp = √[((n1 − 1)s1² + (n2 − 1)s2²) / (n1 + n2 − 2)]

**Working:**
- (n1 − 1)s1² = 14 × 10² = 14 × 100 = **1400**
- (n2 − 1)s2² = 13 × 8² = 13 × 64 = **832**
- Numerator = 1400 + 832 = **2,232**
- Denominator = 15 + 14 − 2 = **27**
- sp² = 2,232/27 ≈ **82.67**, so sp = √82.67 ≈ **9.09 ≈ 9.1**

**Answer:** sp ≈ **9.1**. (The slide prints √82.96, but 2,232/27 is about 82.67; either way sp rounds to 9.1.)

questions.stem: Explain the three types of t-tests, give the formula for each, and state when each should be used.
questions.model_answer_md:
t-tests compare means, and the module covers three versions.

**1. One-sample t-test**
- Compares the **mean of a single group** to a **known or hypothesised population mean**.
- Used when we want to know if **our sample is significantly different from a specific value**.
- **Formula:** t = (x̄ − μ0) / (s/√n), where x̄ is the sample mean, μ0 the hypothesized population mean, s the standard deviation and n the sample size.
- **Example:** sugar in energy bars against the dietician's 15g.

**2. Independent two-sample (unpaired) t-test**
- Compares the **means of two independent groups**.
- Used when samples come from **different populations** (e.g. **Treatment vs Control**); the **groups must be unrelated**.
- **Formula (equal variances):** t = (x̄1 − x̄2) / (sp √(1/n1 + 1/n2)), with pooled SD sp = √[((n1 − 1)s1² + (n2 − 1)s2²) / (n1 + n2 − 2)].
- **Example:** test scores of Class A vs Class B.

**3. Paired (dependent) t-test**
- Compares the means from the **same group at different times (pre/post)** or **matched pairs**.
- Used when **measurements are repeated** or **pairs are naturally linked**.
- **Formula:** compute di = x1,i − x2,i for each pair, then t = d̄ / (sd/√n), where d̄ is the mean of differences, sd their standard deviation and n the number of pairs.
- **Example:** clients' pulse rate before and after a training program.

**Conclusion:** one group vs a value calls for the one-sample test, two unrelated groups for the independent test, and the same subjects measured twice for the paired test.

rubric.point: Independent: two unrelated groups, Treatment vs Control
Paired: same group pre/post or matched pairs

questions.stem: For the deck's three worked t-tests (sugar bars: n = 10, t ≈ −1.58, two-tailed; two classes: n1 = 15, n2 = 14, t ≈ −2.02, two-tailed; pulse rates: 6 pairs, t ≈ 2.69, one-tailed), find the degrees of freedom and the critical t from the t table at α = 0.05, and state each decision.
questions.model_answer_md:
Each test needs its degrees of freedom and the right column of the t table.

**How the deck reads the table:** for a **two-tailed** test at α = 0.05 the worked examples use the **0.025** column; for a **one-tailed** test at α = 0.05 they use the **0.05** column.

**1. Sugar bars (one-sample, two-tailed)**
- df = n − 1 = 10 − 1 = **9**
- Critical t (df 9, 0.025 column) = **±2.685**
- |t| = 1.58 < 2.685, so **fail to reject H0**: no evidence the mean sugar differs from 15g.

**2. Two classes (independent, two-tailed)**
- df = n1 + n2 − 2 = 15 + 14 − 2 = **27**
- Critical t (df 27, 0.025 column) = **±2.373**
- |t| = 2.02 < 2.373, so **fail to reject H0**: no significant difference in mean scores.

**3. Pulse rates (paired, one-tailed)**
- df = n − 1 = 6 − 1 = **5**
- Critical t (df 5, 0.05 column) = **2.571**
- t = 2.69 > 2.571, so **reject H0**: the program reduces pulse rate (the slide's p-value is about 0.021, below 0.05).

**Note:** the slides' decision lines also print older numbers (2.262, 2.052 and 2.015); each decision is the same with either number.

**Conclusion:** only the paired pulse test clears its critical value, so only there is H0 rejected.

rubric.point: Sugar: df 9, critical ±2.685, fail to reject
Classes: df 27, critical ±2.373, fail to reject
